title: Hardware-Accelerated Guardrails
summary: Accelerate selected safety and policy checks while keeping their detection limits, ordering, and failure behavior explicit.
overview: Hardware-accelerated guardrails run suitable classifiers or validation models on optimized inference infrastructure to reduce latency or increase throughput. Examples include content-safety classifiers, topic checks, or specialized input and output detectors. Hardware acceleration changes execution performance; it does not make a classifier complete, correct, or a replacement for deterministic authorization.

The guardrail architecture should separate cheap structural checks, learned classification, and business authorization. Some checks run before generation, some before tool execution, and others before output release. Batching or shared accelerators can improve utilization but may delay critical checks behind model work unless capacity is isolated.

production.poc: A prototype benchmarks the guard model’s detection quality and latency independently from the main model.
production.production: Production versions thresholds and models, defines fail-closed or degraded behavior by action type, and validates checks before streaming release.
production.scale: Enterprise scale reserves guard capacity, monitors false positives and false negatives by task and language, and canaries hardware or precision changes alongside policy evaluation.

components.name: Deterministic validation layer
components.role: Checks schemas, size limits, allowed tools, and authorization independently of model judgment.

components.name: Guard model runtime
components.role: Executes evaluated classifiers on compatible accelerated infrastructure.

components.name: Policy decision service
components.role: Combines signals and determines allow, block, transform, or review outcomes.

components.name: Release and tool gate
components.role: Prevents unapproved content or actions from leaving the relevant boundary.

components.name: Guard telemetry
components.role: Tracks decision quality, latency, saturation, and model or threshold versions.

flow.title: Identify the control boundary
flow.description: Determine whether the check protects input handling, tool execution, or output disclosure.

flow.title: Run deterministic checks
flow.description: Reject invalid schemas and unauthorized operations before spending classifier compute.

flow.title: Classify relevant content
flow.description: Send only the required data to an evaluated guard model under a bounded deadline.

flow.title: Apply policy thresholds
flow.description: Combine classifier output with task risk and documented uncertainty handling.

flow.title: Gate the action or release
flow.description: Allow execution or output only after the required decision is available.

flow.title: Monitor and recalibrate
flow.description: Review sampled errors and latency while keeping policy changes versioned and reversible.

diagrams.title: Accelerated classification inside a broader control system
diagrams.code:
flowchart LR
 R["Agent input or proposed output"] --> D["Deterministic checks"]
 D --> G["Accelerated guard classifier"]
 G --> P["Policy decision"]
 P --> A["Allow release or tool action"]
 P --> B["Block or request review"]
 I["Authoritative permissions"] --> P
 G --> M["Detection and latency metrics"]
diagrams.caption: A fast classifier informs policy; authoritative permissions remain a separate mandatory input.

useCase.title: Checking generated seller-support replies
useCase.situation: A marketplace assistant drafts support replies during high-volume seller events.
useCase.problem: A separate content check adds enough latency to make streaming feel stalled, while bypassing checks is unacceptable.
useCase.requirement: Reduce guard latency without weakening release policy or tool authorization.
useCase.architecture: A compact guard model runs on reserved accelerated capacity and the gateway buffers content until required checks pass.
runtime: The proposed reply passes structural checks and enters the guard classifier.
The policy gate releases approved content or requests review for uncertain cases.
useCase.failure: If guard capacity is unavailable, policy-sensitive output remains buffered or the task returns a controlled unavailable state.
useCase.impact: Measure false-negative and false-positive rates together with guard latency and queue age; faster checks provide no benefit if their release boundary is misplaced.

failures.detection: Main generation finishes while approval waits indefinitely.
failures.recovery: Bound the queue and reserve critical guard capacity.

failures.detection: Detection rates change after an optimized deployment.
failures.recovery: Recalibrate on labeled data and revert the serving bundle if needed.

mistakes.fix: Evaluate detection quality separately from speed.
Enforce permissions in deterministic policy code.

mistakes.mistake: Checking output after it is visible
mistakes.fix: Place the gate before the protected release boundary.

whenToUse: Use when evaluated guard models materially affect latency.
Use for high-throughput services with clear control boundaries.
Use when accelerator efficiency justifies dedicated deployment.
whenNotToUse: Avoid learned checks for simple exact permission decisions.
Do not assume a guard model detects every unsafe case.
Avoid sharing saturated capacity without a failure policy.
checklist: Measure detection errors by task slice.
Test timeout behavior before output release.
